```{r setup}
library(peridial)
```

## Overview

peRidial represents a PD unit as four nested S3 classes. Each class owns the
level below it, so the structure mirrors how the clinical data are recorded:
a unit has patients, a patient has catheters, and a catheter has peritonitis
episodes.

This vignette explains what each class holds, how they fit together, and how
to look inside them. For building a `pd_unit` from files, see
`vignette("peridial")`.

## The hierarchy

```
pd_unit        one PD unit and one reporting period (t0 to t1)
└── pd_patient     one patient
    └── pd_catheter    one PD catheter
        └── pd_infection   one peritonitis episode
```

| Class | One object is... | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `pd_unit` | a unit over a reporting period | its patients, plus unit-level figures such as `n_patients`, `n_new` and `tpyar` |
| `pd_patient` | one patient | demographics and their catheters |
| `pd_catheter` | one PD catheter | insertion and PD start dates, procedure type, and the episodes that occurred on it |
| `pd_infection` | one peritonitis episode | infection date, organism(s), last antibiotic dose, and the episode type |

The reporting period `t0` and `t1` is passed down the hierarchy, so
exposure time is always measured against the same window.

## Building the objects from the bottom up

The constructors follow the hierarchy: episodes first, then the catheter that
owns them, then the patient.

```{r}
t0 <- as.Date("2025-01-01")
t1 <- as.Date("2025-12-31")

ep1 <- pd_infection(
  patient_id = "ABC1234",
  infection_date = as.Date("2025-03-10"),
  organism_list = list("Staphylococcus aureus"),
  last_dose_antibiotic = as.Date("2025-03-31")
)

ep2 <- pd_infection(
  patient_id = "ABC1234",
  infection_date = as.Date("2025-04-15"),
  organism_list = list("Staphylococcus aureus"),
  last_dose_antibiotic = as.Date("2025-05-06"),
  prior_episode = ep1
)

catheter <- pd_catheter(
  patient_id = "ABC1234",
  catheter_id = "ABC1234_01",
  insertion_date = as.Date("2024-11-02"),
  procedure_type = "Laparoscopic",
  pd_start_date = as.Date("2024-11-20"),
  infections = list(ep1, ep2),
  t0 = t0, t1 = t1
)

patient <- pd_patient(
  patient_id = "ABC1234",
  catheters = list(catheter),
  t0 = t0, t1 = t1,
  gender = "Female",
  date_of_birth = as.Date("1961-06-14")
)
```

Each object links to its parent through `patient_id`, and episodes also link
to their catheter through `catheter_id`. Passing `infections = list(ep1, ep2)`
to `pd_catheter()` is what attaches the episodes to the catheter.

## Looking inside an object

Printing gives a summary, and `str()` shows what the object is made of:

```{r}
patient
```

```{r}
str(patient, max.level = 1)
```

Fields are read with `$`, as with `ep2$episode_type` in the introduction.

## Constructors and validation

     it for pd_infection (new_pd_infection() + validate_pd_infection()) and
     new_pd_patient() / pd_patient(). -->

Each class has two layers:

- A low-level constructor, such as `new_pd_infection()`, that assembles the
  object without checking it.
- A user-facing function, such as `pd_infection()`, that builds the object and
  then runs `validate_pd_infection()`.

Use the user-facing functions in your own code. They guarantee that an object
which exists is valid.

## Working with a whole unit as a table

A `pd_unit` built from the example files can be flattened into one table with
`subset()`. It works like base `subset()` and returns a plain tibble. It never
modifies the unit.

```{r}
unit <- pd_unit(
  unit_data_path = system.file("extdata", "a3_2025.xlsx", package = "peridial"),
  infection_data_path = system.file("extdata", "pe_2025.xlsx", package = "peridial"),
  t0 = t0, t1 = t1, unit_id = "Wellington PD Unit"
)
```

The table has one row per episode. Patient, catheter and episode columns sit
side by side, so one condition can use columns from any level. A catheter with
no episodes still gets a row, with `NA` in the episode columns.

```{r}
subset(
  unit,
  gender == "Female" & !is.na(infection_date),
  select = c(patient_id, catheter_id, infection_date)
)
```

A few things to know:

- `subset()` also works on a single `pd_patient` or `pd_catheter`. A
  `pd_catheter` only knows its `patient_id`, so patient columns such as
  `gender` are not available there.
- Stored values such as `n_episodes` and `patient_years_at_risk` describe the
  whole unit. They do not change when rows are filtered.
- To get a single `pd_patient` object out of a unit, search its patient list:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
Find(function(p) p$patient_id == "ABC1234", unit$patient_list)
```
